title: Chapter 9: Communication and Persuading Consumer
text: Chapter Nine Communication and Persuading Consumer. Consumer Behavior, Twelfth Edition, Global Edition (Schiffman & Wisenblit).

title: Which Type of Communication Is Featured in This Ad?
text: Which Type of Communication Is Featured in This Ad, and What Strategic Concept Does It Get Across? HSBC ad: the same hand gesture means "Be patient" in Egypt, "What exactly do you mean?" in Italy, and "That's just perfect" in Greece. "Never underestimate the importance of local knowledge." HSBC - The world's local bank.

title: Basic Communication Model
text: Basic Communication Model. Sender (Source) encodes the Message, which travels through a Channel (Medium) to the Receiver (Consumer), who decodes it. Feedback flows from the receiver back to the sender.

title: The Source as the Initiator
text: The Source as the Initiator. Formal Communication Source: a marketer or organization. Informal Source: a parent, friend or other consumer.

title: The Source – Impersonal and Interpersonal Communications
text: The Source - Impersonal and Interpersonal Communications. Source Credibility. Reference Groups: Normative, Comparative, Membership → Symbolic. Example shown: the Harley-Davidson logo.

title: The Source – Informal Sources and Word of Mouth
text: The Source - Informal Sources and Word of Mouth. Informal Sources: Opinion leaders. Word of Mouth and eWOM: Two-way communication; Social networks; Brand communities; Message boards and Blogs.

title: The Source – Word of Mouth: Strategic Applications
text: The Source - Word of Mouth: Strategic Applications. Buzz agents. Viral marketing. Tackling negative rumors.

title: The Source – Credibility of Formal Sources
text: The Source - Credibility of Formal Sources. Institutional advertising. Publicity. Endorsers. Chart: the Davie Brown Index (DBI) celebrity ranking (Tom Hanks #1, Will Smith #2, Angelina Jolie #12, Jennifer Lopez #64, Dale Earnhardt Jr. #195, Shania Twain #262, Mick Jagger #361, Jessica Alba #439).

title: The Right Stuff: The Davie Brown Index
text: The Right Stuff. The Davie Brown Index, a celebrity hot list, uses consumer awareness and seven other metrics, including likeability and trendsetting ability, to score marketing potential. DBI score by ranking: Tom Hanks #1, Will Smith #2, Angelina Jolie #12, Jennifer Lopez #64, Dale Earnhardt Jr. #195, Shania Twain #262, Mick Jagger #361, Jessica Alba #439.

title: Why Are Consumers Likely to Perceive This Ad as Credible?
text: Why Are Consumers Likely to Perceive This Ad as Credible? Adidas ad featuring Lionel Messi in the Argentina national team shirt.

title: Credibility of Formal Sources: Endorser Effectiveness
text: Credibility of Formal Sources: Endorser Effectiveness. Effectiveness is related to the message and its ease of comprehension. Synergy between the endorser and the product types is important. Endorser's demographic characteristics (e.g. age and social class) should be similar to the target audience. Endorser credibility is not a substitute for corporate credibility. Endorser's words must be realistic.

title: The Receivers as the Target Audience
text: The Receivers as the Target Audience. Personal characteristics and motives. Involvement and congruency. Mood. Barriers to communication: Selective exposure to messages; Psychological noise.

title: Overcoming Psychological Noise
text: Overcoming Psychological Noise. Repeating exposure to advertising messages. Contrast to break through clutter. Customized promotion messages. Effective positioning. Offering unique value propositions.

title: Media as Channels for Transmitting Messages
text: Media as Channels for transmitting messages. Mass Media vs. Nontraditional (New) Media. New media is: Addressable - customized and addressed to different receivers. Interactive - receivers can interact with the sender. Response measurable - the receiver's response can be measured.

title: The Shift From Traditional To Nontraditional Advertising
text: The Shift From Traditional To Nontraditional Advertising. Chart: share of U.S. ad spending by medium, 2000-2020 (Zenith). The internet passed TV in 2017 to become the biggest U.S. ad medium. Internet 3.8% in 2000 to 44.7% in 2020; TV 33.4% to 30.6%; Newspaper 31.1% to about 6%; Magazine 15.3% to about 6%; Radio 13.3% to 8.1%; Out of home 3.1% to 5.1%.

title: Gender-Based Marketing
text: Gender-Based Marketing. Marketing Communications: the top social media sites for men and women (Women % / Men %): Facebook 77 / 61; Pinterest 46 / 16; Instagram 44 / 36; Snapchat 28 / 22; LinkedIn 26 / 31; TikTok 24 / 17; Twitter 22 / 25; WhatsApp 21 / 26. Source: Pew Research, Social Media Use in 2021.

title: Nontraditional Media
text: Nontraditional Media. Out-of-home and On-the-go: advertising screens in buildings and transit vehicles (e.g. taxis, trains and buses); digital billboards on roads; ambient advertising (experiential advertising). Online and Mobile: includes consumer-generated media; narrowcast messages; interactive TV (iTV).

title: Media and Message Congruence
text: Media and message congruence. Addressable advertising: a highly customized message directly to a single viewer. Branded entertainment: product placement.

title: Designing Persuasive Communications: Wordplay
text: Designing Persuasive Communications - Message Structure and Presentation. Advertising Resonance; Message framing; One-Sided versus Two-Sided Messages; Order Effects. Advertising Resonance - Wordplay: used to create a double meaning when used with a relevant picture.

title: Which Advertising Technique Is Used in Each Ad?
text: Which Advertising Technique Is Used in Each Ad, and How So? Tabasco ad: the sauce bottle drawn as a hand grenade - "Explode your sense. Little bottle, big flavor."

title: Example: Volkswagen Park Assist
text: Volkswagen ad: goldfish in plastic water bags lined up beside a hedgehog - "Precision Parking. Park Assist by Volkswagen."

title: Designing Persuasive Communications: Message Framing
text: Designing Persuasive Communications - Message Structure and Presentation. Message framing: Positive framing; Negative framing.

title: Example: Message Framing
text: Two frozen yoghurt cups with the same fact framed two ways: "Contains 20% fat" (negative framing) versus "80% fat free" (positive framing).

title: Designing Persuasive Communications: One-Sided vs Two-Sided
text: Designing Persuasive Communications - Message Structure and Presentation. One-Sided versus Two-Sided Messages: the choice depends on the nature of the audience and the nature of the competition.

title: Example: Cigarette Pack Warnings
text: Two cigarette packs: a Marlboro pack with the text warning "Smoking kills", and a French Marlboro Gold pack with a graphic photo and the warning "Fumer provoque des crises cardiaques" (smoking causes heart attacks).

title: One- versus Two-Sided Messages
text: One- versus Two-Sided Messages. Clorox ad: "Which dog has more spots?" and "Which sock is whiter?" - leading detergent alone versus leading detergent plus Clorox Bleach. "Obviously."

title: Designing Persuasive Communications: Order Effects
text: Designing Persuasive Communications - Message Structure and Presentation. Order Effects: Primacy (first ad); Recency (last ad); Brand name.

title: Advertising Appeals
text: Advertising Appeals: Comparative; Fear; Humor; Abrasive; Sex; Audience participation; Timely; Celebrities.

title: Example: Comparative Appeal (Audi vs BMW)
text: Comparative advertising billboards: Audi - "Your move, BMW." BMW's reply billboard - "Checkmate."

title: Comparative
text: Comparative. Ad still: "Built Ford Proud".

title: Example: Comparative Ads
text: Two comparative ads: soup cans compared side by side - Progresso "Bring your dictionary" versus Campbell's Select Harvest "Bring your appetite" (long versus simple ingredient lists); and Carnation evaporated milk - milk "For cookies" versus Carnation "For cooks".

title: Humor Appeals
text: Humor Appeals. Mercedes-Benz ad: "Unofficial service can be dangerous." A wrench whose shadow looks like a monster's open jaws. "15% discount on spare parts and free vehicle diagnosis."

title: Example: Humor Appeal (Lay's)
text: Lay's chip bags (Chili, Tomato Ketchup) designed as faces with wide-open mouths - UEFA Champions League edition, Arabic packaging.

title: Fear Appeals
text: Fear Appeals. When do they work? When are they unlikely to work? Ad: a fist made of dynamite sticks with a lit fuse - "The longer you wait, the deadlier abuse gets." (family peace center).

title: Abrasive Advertising
text: Abrasive advertising. Burger King's Moldy Whopper Ad.

title: Types of Celebrity Appeals
text: Types of Celebrity Appeals. Testimonial: based on personal usage, a celebrity attests to the quality of the product or service. Endorsement: the celebrity lends his or her name and appears on behalf of a product or service with which he or she may or may not be an expert. Actor: the celebrity presents a product or service as part of a character endorsement. Spokesperson: the celebrity represents the brand or company over an extended period of time.

title: Example: Celebrity Appeal (TAG Heuer)
text: TAG Heuer watch ad featuring Leonardo DiCaprio.

title: Feedback: Determining Effectiveness
text: Feedback - Determining Effectiveness. Exposure effects: how many consumers received the message? Persuasion effects: was the message received and interpreted correctly? Sales effects: did the ads increase sales?
